The exact current marker is INTERVIEW-76-f4008c75c646104c. The screen asks for JavaScript solve(n) to count non-attacking arrangements of n queens, with n ≤ 10, returning the count without stdin/stdout, imports, or exports.

Use row-by-row backtracking, tracking occupied columns and diagonals identified by row − column and row + column. The invariant is that before searching row r, rows 0 through r − 1 contain exactly one queen each, all mutually non-attacking, and the tracking sets describe exactly those queens. Try every safe column, mark its column and diagonals, recurse, then undo those marks; reaching row n contributes one arrangement, and a dead end contributes zero. Every valid board has one unique row-by-row placement sequence, so it is counted exactly once.

Boundary cases: n = 0 returns 1 for the empty arrangement; n = 1 returns 1; n = 2 or 3 returns 0. Auxiliary space is O(n), with O(n · n!) as a conservative time upper bound. No implementation yet.

Approach: use iterative DFS or BFS with two colors. Start a traversal from every uncolored vertex, assign each uncolored neighbor the opposite color, and return false if an edge connects vertices with the same color. Return true once all components have been checked.

Invariant: every discovered vertex has one assigned color, and every checked edge connects opposite colors unless a conflict has already caused rejection. Mark vertices when pushing or enqueueing them so they are discovered only once.
